title: Medical-equipment suppliers that rose fast, live on one item, or share an address with the provider who orders
question: Which Bay Area suppliers of medical equipment and supplies grew suddenly, are paid almost wholly for one item that few others supply, or are supplied from the same address as the provider who orders the item?
finding: Medicare paid 696 Bay Area suppliers $85.1 million in 2024. 7 of those paid $250,000 or more show at least one of the patterns ($16.2 million between them). The largest is Medicare Drop LLC, Campbell: $10.9 million in 2024, first in the file in 2021, mainly for wheelchair accessory, power seating system, combination tilt and… (code E1007). 2 are supplied from the address of the provider who orders: the largest is Sah Orthopaedic Associates, Fremont, paid $1.9 million for collagen dressing, sterile, size more than 48 sq. in., each (code A6023), where Alexander Sah, MD (provider no. 1003966359), at the same street address, ordered $1.8 million of this item from 1 supplier. 6 first appear in the file in 2022 or later, or grew past $5 million after 2018.
how: From the federal files of Medicare payments for durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies, 2018 to 2024, Bay Area suppliers only. A supplier paid $250,000 or more in 2024 is listed when (1) it first appears in 2022 or later and was paid $500,000 or more, or its payments more than tripled in a year, or it reached $5 million after first appearing later than 2018; (2) at least 80% of its payments are for one item and it takes at least half of all Bay Area payments for that item; or (3) a provider at the same street address, or with the same provider number, ordered at least half the dollar value of the supplier's main item. Payment per patient is set against the middle Bay Area supplier of the same federal supplier type. The address-cluster note comes from the existing address screen.
limits: The federal files do not say which provider sent a patient to which supplier, so "ordered at the same address" is two totals that match, not a traced referral. A doctor's office that supplies items to its own patients, and a device maker that bills Medicare directly for a device only it makes, both produce these patterns; whether a given arrangement is allowed turns on rules that are not in these files. A new provider number can be an old business under a new owner. The files hold Bay Area rows only, so there is no national figure per item on disk; "share of Bay Area payments" is small-sample by nature. Rows with fewer than 11 patients are withheld by the publisher, so item totals are lower bounds.
